items.statement: For any vertex cover C of size c in a graph T on n vertices, with N=n-c, the decomposition over independent X subset C gives Delta_r(T) >= d_r(N)+sum_{a=1}^{min(c,r+1)} binom(c,a)m_N(r-a), where d_s(b)=binom(b,s+1)-binom(b,s) with zero extension and m_N(s)=min_{0<=b<=N}d_s(b). Therefore eligibility x(T)+2<=p requires this lower bound to be negative for some 0<=r<=p-2.
items.replay: Expand I_T(z)=sum_X z^|X|(1+z)^b_X, subtract coefficients of z^r and z^(r+1), bound each nonempty-X contribution by the finite minimum over b=0,...,N, and use that eligibility supplies an integer negative Delta_r at a rank r<=p-2.

items.statement: For H=T-{v,s}, W=N_T(s)\{v}, k=p-1, and first-mark residuals J_i=H-(N_H[w_i] union earlier marks), q_(k+1)-q_k=sum_i(i_k(J_i)-i_(k-1)(J_i)). If every |V(J_i)|<=2k-1, incidence counting gives each summand nonpositive. For |V(T)|=2p+2+d this follows when an ordering of W makes every deletion union have size at least d+3.
items.replay: Partition marked independent sets by first included mark; after choosing w_i, the remaining vertices lie in J_i. For a graph J, count incidences (A,y) where A is independent of size k-1 and y extends it to an independent k-set: k*i_k(J)<= (|V(J)|-k+1)*i_(k-1)(J). Since |V(J)|<=2k-1, the multiplier is at most k.
